meta.name: SP-404MK2 modulation suggestions
meta.note: Opinions, not MIDI facts. The map JSON stays the source of truth for CCs and ranges; this file only says which parameters are worth moving and how. Every param name here is validated against effects_parameters at build time.
meta.rate_units: Hz for free-running moves. Suggestions that are rhythmic also carry a 'sync' note division: the app uses it when the SP is sending clock (MIDI Sync Out = ON), locking phase to the unit's own downbeat, and falls back to the typed tempo otherwise.
meta.depth_units: percent of the parameter's full CC range, applied either side of the knob's current value when bipolar

shapes.label: Tri
shapes.best_for: continuous ranges — linear up and down, no dwell at the extremes

shapes.label: Sqr
shapes.best_for: switches and rhythmic gates — the only shape that crosses a threshold cleanly

shapes.label: S&H
shapes.best_for: lists and discrete types — holds a random value per step

Slicer.summary: The strongest case on the unit: 32 discrete slice patterns that no hand can step through in time.

suggest.why: A new slice pattern every two beats. Hitting one of 32 detents on cue is not a human action.
Ramps the slice rate up over ~16 seconds — an automated build.
Flips LEGATO/SLASH in rhythm, so the slice envelope changes character bar to bar.

Scatter.summary: Every parameter is discrete, so this wants stepped and square, never sine.

suggest.why: A different scatter pattern each step — the move the effect is built for.
Gates the whole effect on the beat instead of holding it on.
Random single/double-time bursts.

DJFX Delay.summary: The loop switch is the instrument here; everything else supports it.

suggest.why: Rhythmic loop stutter, engaged and released on the beat.
Varies the stutter length so the repeat never settles.

DJFX Looper.summary: A loop switch and a bipolar speed — made for stepped modulation.

suggest.why: Beat-locked loop stabs.
Jumps between forward and reverse playback — a scratch you cannot perform.

Back Spin.summary: A one-shot gesture effect, which is exactly what a square wave automates.

suggest.why: Fires the spin every two seconds instead of by hand.
Randomises the spin length so repeats do not sound copied.

Hyper-Reso.summary: Pitched resonance with a scale — stepped modulation turns it into an arpeggiator.

suggest.why: Steps through scale degrees on the beat: an arpeggio the SP has no other way to make.
Very slow modal shifts under a drone.
Breathes brightness and detune through the resonance.

Resonator.summary: Same idea as Hyper-Reso but chord-based.

suggest.why: Jumps the resonant root — melodic scatter over whatever you feed it.
Rotates the chord shape every few bars.
Swings the resonance across the stereo field.

Ko-Da-Ma.summary: A tempo-locked delay whose time is a list of note values, so stepping it is musical by construction.

suggest.why: Jumps the delay between note values — the classic dub time-shift, on a timer.
Toggles centre and ping-pong so the repeats move around.

Zan-Zou.summary: Multi-tap delay: the tap mode is the character.

suggest.why: Steps the delay time between note values.
Cycles 2/3/4-tap, changing the rhythm of the repeats.

SX Delay.summary: Three parameters, one of which is a list of note values.

suggest.why: Note-value jumps you cannot dial by hand mid-bar.
Slowly swells and drains the repeats.

Sync Delay.summary: Tempo-locked delay, so stepping the time lands on the grid.

suggest.why: Steps between note divisions.
A slow feedback swell that never quite runs away.

TimeCtrlDly.summary: Delay time is the pitch control here — moving it bends the repeats.

suggest.why: Stepped time changes pitch-shift the tail on every jump.
Swells the repeats without touching the knob.

Lo-fi.summary: Nine degradation types is a list worth stepping through.

suggest.why: A different flavour of destruction every few seconds.
Opens and closes the lo-fi filter underneath it.

Isolator.summary: Three-band kill: square waves on these are a DJ move, not an experiment.

suggest.why: Drops the bass on the beat — the isolator cut, automated.
Counter-phased against LOW so the bands trade places.

Harmony.summary: The harmony interval is a list, which is where the interest is.

suggest.why: Rotates the harmony interval so the part rewrites itself.
Slides the vocal character while the pitch holds.

Vocoder.summary: Note and chord are lists; formant is the texture.

suggest.why: Steps the vocoder pitch on the beat — melody from a spoken source.
Rotates the chord voicing every few bars.
Slow gender morph under the melody.

Auto Pitch.summary: Correction becomes an instrument once the settings move.

suggest.why: Slow formant slide — the voice changes character, not pitch.
Snaps in and out of full robot on a timer.

Chromatic PS.summary: Two independent pitch voices with independent pans.

suggest.why: Steps voice 1 through intervals — an arpeggio over any source.
Swings voice 1 across the field.
Counter-phased, so the two voices cross in the middle.

Cloud Delay.summary: Granular by nature, so scattered modulation suits it.

suggest.why: Scatters the grain pitch — clouds instead of echoes.
Thickens and thins the cloud over ~16 seconds.

JUNO Chorus.summary: Only the mode list is worth automating.

suggest.why: Rotates through the JUNO/JX voicings slowly.

Gt Amp Sim.summary: Wild rather than subtle, but the amp list is genuinely fun to step.

suggest.why: Swaps the amp every few seconds — a different rig per phrase.
Slow gain swell underneath.

Super Filter.summary: The obvious one, and its own LFO section sits on CTRL 4-6 where your hands cannot reach.

suggest.why: The sweep everyone wants, held perfectly steady for as long as you like.
Counter-phased against cutoff, so resonance peaks as the filter closes.
Jumps LPF/BPF/HPF in rhythm — impossible to do cleanly by hand.

Filter+Drive.summary: Filter plus saturation: move the cutoff and the drive follows it.

suggest.why: Classic sweep, steady over minutes.
Peaks as the filter closes.
Flips high-pass and low-pass on a timer.

Tape Echo.summary: The dub move is the tape speed, and holding it steady by hand is the hard part.

suggest.why: A 20-second drift that pitch-bends every repeat — tape slowing and recovering.
Breathes the wow and flutter in and out.
Rotates the playback-head combination, changing the echo pattern.

Wah.summary: A pedal you do not have to keep your foot on.

suggest.why: The sweep itself, at a rate no ankle holds steady.
Accelerates the auto-wah into a build.

Phaser.summary: Manual is the sweep position; rate is the sweep speed.

suggest.why: Slow jet sweep through the notches.
Speeds the phaser up over ~20 seconds.

Flanger.summary: Same shape as the phaser, more metallic.

suggest.why: Moves the flange peak through the source.
An accelerating jet.

Chorus.summary: Its rate is in seconds, so modulating the rate is the interesting part.

suggest.why: Wobbles the chorus speed — detune that never settles.
Thickens and thins the chorus.
Sweeps the sidebands — the classic sci-fi glide.
Flips the modulation direction on the beat.
Slides the band spacing so the comb walks through the source.
Jumps between the six filter ranges.

Crusher.summary: Degradation with a rate control, which is what to automate.

suggest.why: Ramps sample-rate destruction into a build.
Sweeps the post-crush filter to keep it musical.

Ha-Dou.summary: Depth and time are both continuous and both change the character.

suggest.why: Breathes the effect depth.
Slowly stretches and shortens the effect.

Tremolo/Pan.summary: An LFO effect whose own rate is the thing worth automating.

suggest.why: Accelerating tremolo — a build with no hands on it.
Rotates the LFO wave, so the tremolo changes shape.
Fades the effect in and out.

Reverb.summary: Space that breathes rather than sits.

suggest.why: A 25-second swell of the room size.
Darkens and brightens the tail.

SX Reverb.summary: Three controls; time is the one worth moving.

suggest.why: Slow expansion and collapse of the space.
Counter-phased, so the tail darkens as it lengthens.

Downer.summary: A pitch dive with its own rate — square it for rhythm.

suggest.why: Dives on the beat instead of when you turn a knob.
Sweeps the high-frequency loss under the dive.
A stop every two seconds, exactly on time.
Shortens the stop over a build.

To-Gu-Ro.summary: The same family, with filter and amp modulation of its own.

suggest.why: Rhythmic slowdowns.
Tightens the cycle over time.

Cassette Sim.summary: Texture, but the age control is a genuinely fun slow move.

suggest.why: Ages and un-ages the tape over half a minute.
Varies the instability instead of leaving it fixed.

404 VinylSim.summary: The vinyl filter is a continuous sweep.

suggest.why: The record warping in and out of focus.
Uneven platter speed rather than a constant.
Varying instability keeps it from sounding looped.

Equalizer.summary: Rhythmic EQ cuts are an isolator move; the sweep is the subtler one.

suggest.why: Scoops the mids on the beat.
Sweeps the mid band through the source.

Distortion.summary: Gain staging, so only a slow swell earns automation.

suggest.why: Builds and releases saturation over ~20 seconds.
A slow push into breakup and back.

Compressor.summary: Set and forget. Sustain, attack, ratio and level are gain staging — modulating them is noise, not music.

WrmSaturator.summary: Set and forget. Drive and two EQ bands you dial once and leave.
